scope: Proposition 3.1 (Finite plus construction) of the manuscript “A Counterexample to Wall's D(2) Problem” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Walls-D2-Problem-October-6-2026/wall-d2-counterexample.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 321 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e34de3716e64bba4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let B be a finite connected CW complex of dimension at most two, with π1(B) = P. Suppose that the normal closure K of elements t1, . . . , tr ∈ P is perfect, and put G = P/K. There is a finite complex X ⊇ B, obtained by attaching r cells of dimension two and r cells of dimension three, such that: (i) the inclusion induces the quotient P → G on fundamental groups; (ii) Hi( e X; Z) = 0 for every i > 2, and H3(X; M) = 0 for every left ZG-module M; (iii) for every right ZG-module N, the inclusion induces H∗(B; N) ∼ = H∗(X; N), with the coeffi- cients on B pulled back along P → G.
